title: Opalite Health vs. Voyce
summary: Compare Opalite Health vs. Voyce/Martti on AI vs. live medical interpretation, connection time, language coverage, Epic workflows.
body_markdown:
###


Opalite removes the interpreter-matching step entirely for supported spoken languages. That matters most for frequent short interactions, after-hours care, patient calls, and other situations where staff may need interpretation many times a day.


###


The numbers measure different things. Voyce/Martti's figure reflects its human interpreter network, while Opalite's 150+ languages and dialects are available through AI directly. The practical question is which languages need to be available immediately without human matching.


###


Voyce/Martti can document that an interpreter session occurred. Opalite can use the multilingual conversation itself to draft clinical documentation for provider review, so interpretation and note creation can happen in the same workflow.


###


Short bedside interactions, medication review, patient calls, telehealth, after-hours requests, and high-volume ambulatory visits are useful tests because they show whether removing the interpreter-connection step changes staff behavior and access.


###


Long encounters often include pauses while clinicians review the chart, wait for results, document, or speak with other staff. Opalite does not charge for hold time or silent minutes, so those pauses do not add interpretation cost.
